news.title: Sierra Leone U-15 national team arrive in Azerbaijan for FIFA U-15 World Cup
news.lede: The Sierra Leone U-15 delegation has safely arrived in Baku, Azerbaijan, ahead of the FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival. The delegation is headed by Sierra Leone Football Association (SLFA) Executive Committee Member, MBOGBA Joseph Benedict as the young Leone Stars prepare to represent the nation on the international stage. Sierra Leone will face Afghanistan, Djibouti, Russia, Sudan, and Turkey during the tournament and festival. The competition presents an important opportunity for the young players to showcase their talents, gain international experience, and promote Sierra Leone football.

news.title: India squad for FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026: Bibiano Fernandes names 14-player team
news.lede: AIFF Media AIFF Media https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/5zj80c/article71606212.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/India-U15-Mens-National-Team--800x500.png As part of its preparations for the tournament, India played two friendlies against Aspire Academy U-15, which forms the core of the Qatar national team, in Doha last week. Chennai India Under-15 men’s team head coach Bibiano Fernandes has named a 14-player squad for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026, which will be held in Baku, Azerbaijan from October 24 to 31. The Blue Colts will compete in Group K alongside Bahrain, Cameroon, Grenada, Laos and Senegal. As part of their preparations, India played two friendly matches against Aspire Academy U-15, which forms the core of the Qatar national team, in Doha last week.

news.title: NZ Football in line for NZ$42.5 million windfall under FIFA’s new funding plan
news.lede: NZ Football could receive an unprecedented US$25 million (about NZ$42.5 million) over four years under a proposed FIFA funding programme. The world governing body have outlined plans to distribute US$6.35 billion (NZ$10.8 billion) in football development funding between 2027 and 2030. The proposal would more than double FIFA’s previously planned investment, providing increased financial support to all 211 Member Associations, including New Zealand. Each national association would become eligible for US$25 million (NZ$42.5 million), compared with the US$10 million (NZ$17 million) previously planned.

news.title: FIFA Bans Egypt Coach Hossam Hassan for Three Matches Over Conduct at 2026 World Cup
news.lede: (FILE) The Egyptian team will face its upcoming official engagements without its main coaching staff following the suspensions imposed on the coach and the sports director. The ruling came from FIFA’s Disciplinary Committee more than three months after the match. The sanction is based on his conduct on the field and at the post-match press conference. After a goal for his side was disallowed, Hassan crossed his arms in protest in front of the broadcast cameras.
